userStories.title: Gated runner enrollment create, redeemed with the token
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Gate runner enrollment creation with the existing redeem engine and deliver its one-time token only to the executing caller.

**Motivation** — These 8 routes take or return a secret, so 5b to 5d-2 left them ungated, and 6a built redeem for them.

**Approach** — Each command stores and hashes a redacted input, answers the raw result to the redeeming caller, and stores a `toResult` projection without the secret. As in 6a, a human caller always executes at once. An agent waits only where a policy, or the catalog default, asks it to.

| Story | Route | Key | Scope | Variant | Input | `redact` | Run | `toResult` |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| US-001 | `POST /fleet/enrollments` | `fleet.enrollment.create` | null | `rest:fleet-enrollments.create` | `{ labels }` (`parseBody(CreateEnrollmentDto, …)`, `labels ?? []`) | none (stored whole) | `enrollments.create(principal.id, input.labels)` | `({ token, ...rest }) => rest` |

Each handler keeps its `@Requires`, `@HttpCode` and `@ApiResponse`s. It gains `@ApprovalGated({ redeem: true })` and an `@ApprovalRedeemHeader() redeem?: string` parameter (last; `approvals/route/approval-redeem-header.decorator.ts`, as 6a's handlers use: `@Headers(APPROVAL_REDEEM_HEADER)` would make swagger document a second, required header). It has 6a's shape:

```ts
const outcome = await this.routeGate.run<EnrollmentCreatedDto>({
  key: 'fleet.enrollment.create', variant: ENROLLMENT_ROUTE_VARIANTS.create, projectId: null,
  input: { labels: dto.labels ?? [] }, redeem,
});
if (outcome.status === 'pending') throw new ApprovalPending(outcome.request);
return JsonResponse.Ok(outcome.result);
```

- **The enrollment actor stays as today.** `EnrollmentService.create(actorId, labels)` records its activity row with `actorType: 'USER'` even for an agent. Fixing that is out of scope.
- **Each route story removes its own rows** from `PENDING_GATE_ROUTES` and `SECRET_GATE_ROUTES`, and sets the exact counts to its own state. US-007 deletes both.

Add ENROLLMENT_ROUTE_VARIANTS.create in fleet/runners/runner-route.commands.ts and register it through RunnerRouteCommands, appending EnrollmentService to its constructor. The command loads the principal via ActorPrincipalLoader. Append ApprovalRouteGate to EnrollmentsController's constructor; remove create's principal parameter. Preserve existing runner registrations and enrollment read behavior. Update every RunnerRouteCommands unit construction with the last service double and extend registration, projection and controller assertions. This high-risk key keeps catalog default agent, so agent calls wait even without policy. Remove only POST /fleet/enrollments from both rollout lists; update exact pending counts/titles to 7 and booted gated-route count/title to 119 in the two shared permission-contract specs. Add test/integration/fleet/gated-enrollment-create-route.integration.spec.ts using the established HTTP redeem fixture pattern. Each test repeats its own setup; a requesting agent holds only global fleet.enrollment.create, with PermissionCache invalidated after binding.

**Scope** — In: enrollment route/registration, one-time token projection, regression tests and the 7/119 rollout checkpoint. Out: VCS gates/helper (US-002/003), webhook gates (US-004), invite gates (US-005), project CI-token variant (US-006), final allowlist deletion/OpenAPI regeneration (US-007); Fixing `EnrollmentService.create`'s hard-coded activity `actorType: 'USER'` for an agent caller.

**Interface** — `EnrollmentsController.create(dto, redeem?)` (the command loads the principal itself); `ENROLLMENT_ROUTE_VARIANTS.create` in `fleet/runners/runner-route.commands.ts`; `EnrollmentService.create(actorId, labels)` remains unchanged.

userStories.title: Gated VCS connection create with the token redacted
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Gate VCS connection creation, redact approved token input and keep polling refresh safely outside the redeem transaction.

**Motivation** — These 8 routes take or return a secret, so 5b to 5d-2 left them ungated, and 6a built redeem for them.

**Approach** —
- **One redaction helper.** `redactSecret(value)` (new, `approvals/route/redact-secret.ts`) answers `REDACTED_SECRET` (`'<redacted>'`) for a string and the value itself otherwise (`undefined`, `null`). Every redact in this feature maps its secret fields through it. A redeem then matches the approved call field for field:
  - an approval of "change `syncMode`" stores no `token` key, so a redemption that adds a `token` hashes differently and answers 409 `approvals.redeemMismatch`;
  - an approval of "set a token" stores `token: '<redacted>'`, so the redemption may carry any token value, as 6a's password does.
- **VCS create and update refresh polling after commit.** Both await `this.vcsPollingService.refreshConnectionSchedule(id)` inline today. Inside a redeem execution that call would run before the commit and read the row through another connection. Both call a private `refreshAfterCommit(id)` instead:
  - it defers the refresh with `AfterCommitService.defer` (as 6a's `AgentsService.invalidateAfterCommit` does);
  - when `defer` answers false (no scope open: the immediate path), it awaits the refresh at once, as today;
  - the deferred task catches a refresh error and logs it as a warning through a class logger (`private readonly logger = new Logger(VcsConnectionService.name)`, per `.nax/rules/api-logging.md`), so a failed schedule refresh after commit never turns a redemption that already executed into a 500 that loses the one-time `webhookSecret`. The immediate path keeps today's propagation.

  `committedEffect` is not used: it takes a synchronous effect and would drop the awaited refresh. `VcsConnectionService`'s constructor gains `AfterCommitService` (last), resolved from the global `PermissionsModule`.
- **The encryption key stays a route precondition.** The VCS create and update handlers keep refusing a missing `vcsConfig.encryptionKey` (400 `vcs`) before the gate. The update handler's order is `findBySlug` → key check → `findByProject` → gate, so a missing key answers 400 before a missing connection answers 404. The commands read `this.vcsConfig.encryptionKey` when they run, and throw the same 400 when it is missing then.

| Story | Route | Key | Scope | Variant | Input | `redact` | Run | `toResult` |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| US-002 | `POST /projects/:slug/vcs` | `vcs.connection.create` | project | `rest:vcs.create` | `{ slug, projectId, connection: parseBody(CreateVcsConnectionDto, …) }` | `connection.token` → `redactSecret` | `vcs.create(projectId, key, connection)` | `({ webhookSecret, ...rest }) => rest` |

`key` in the VCS rows is `this.vcsConfig.encryptionKey`, read when the command runs. Each handler keeps its `@Requires`, `@HttpCode` and `@ApiResponse`s. It gains `@ApprovalGated({ redeem: true })` and an `@ApprovalRedeemHeader() redeem?: string` parameter (last; `approvals/route/approval-redeem-header.decorator.ts`, as 6a's handlers use: `@Headers(APPROVAL_REDEEM_HEADER)` would make swagger document a second, required header).

Add VCS_ROUTE_VARIANTS.create to the existing registrar, preserving delete/test/sync commands. Preserve create's projectsService.findBySlug lookup and encryption-key precondition, then gate { slug, projectId, connection } and return raw results through JsonResponse.Ok. Create/redemption responds 201 with the generated webhookSecret but stored results omit it; high/default-agent means no-policy agent calls wait. Implement the shared helper and its unit spec now for downstream stories. In this story only create switches to refreshAfterCommit; update switches in US-003. Append AfterCommitService to all VcsConnectionService constructions: source vcs-connection.service.spec.ts, integration vcs-connection.service.spec.ts, vcs-connection.webhook-secret.spec.ts, vcs-connection.gitlab.spec.ts and approval-execution.service.spec.ts. GlobalStubsModule already provides AfterCommitService. Update both vcs.controller.spec.ts and test/integration/vcs/vcs-controller.spec.ts gate doubles to execute rest:vcs.create as mockVcsService.create(call.input.projectId, encryptionKey, call.input.connection), preserving their existing argument assertions. Add create registration/redaction/config checks to vcs-route.commands.spec.ts and deferred/immediate-refresh assertions to service unit coverage. Create test/integration/vcs/gated-vcs-secret-routes.integration.spec.ts; stub VCS_ENCRYPTION_KEY before app boot and clean each project's connection beforeEach. Bind project.read and vcs.connection.create to the agent on the test project, then invalidate PermissionCache. Remove only POST /projects/:slug/vcs from both rollout sets and update exact contract counts/titles to pending 6/gated 120.

**Scope** — In: shared redaction primitive, VCS create gate, create polling transaction boundary, constructor compatibility and the 6/120 checkpoint. Out: VCS update/rotation gates and their connection pinning (US-003), webhook prepare (US-004), invite commands (US-005), project token command (US-006), final closure/OpenAPI artifact (US-007). Do not change catalog defaults or use committedEffect for awaited refresh.

**Interface** — `redactSecret(value)`; `REDACTED_SECRET`; `VCS_ROUTE_VARIANTS.create`; `VcsController.createConnection(slug, dto, redeem?)`; `VcsConnectionService` constructor gains `AfterCommitService` (last); private `refreshAfterCommit(id)`.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [unit] redactSecret('s') and redactSecret('') return '<redacted>', redactSecret(null) returns null, redactSecret(undefined) returns undefined, and REDACTED_SECRET equals '<redacted>'.

AC-2 [integration] When an agent holding project-scoped vcs.connection.create and project.read POSTs /api/projects/<slug>/vcs under no policy with { provider: 'github', repoOwner: 'acme', repoName: <unique>, token: 'tok-1', syncMode: 'off' }, then the response is 202 with data matching { permissionKey: 'vcs.connection.create', redeem: true }, and the project has no VcsConnection.

AC-4 [integration] When an approved VCS create request is redeemed, then the response is 201 with data.webhookSecret a non-empty string and data.repoName equal to the opening body's, while the request row's result has no webhookSecret property.

AC-5 [integration] When an approved VCS create request opened with token tok-1 is redeemed with token tok-2, then it answers 201 and its stored encryptedToken decrypts with decryptToken and the stubbed encryption key to tok-2.
AC-6 [integration] When an approved VCS create request is redeemed with another repoName, then it answers 409 with key approvals.redeemMismatch and the project has no VcsConnection.
AC-7 [integration] When POST /api/projects/<slug>/vcs uses the root token, then it answers 201 with a data.webhookSecret and writes no ApprovalRequest row.

AC-8 [unit] After VcsRouteCommands.onModuleInit, registry.get('vcs.connection.create', 'rest:vcs.create') returns a command with key 'vcs.connection.create' and a redeem object whose redact({ slug: 's', projectId: 'p1', connection: { provider: 'github', repoOwner: 'o', repoName: 'r', token: 't' } }) returns the same input with connection.token '<redacted>'.
AC-9 [unit] The rest:vcs.create command's execute rejects with ValidationAppException carrying key vcs when vcsConfig.encryptionKey is empty and never calls VcsConnectionService.create.

AC-10 [unit] VcsConnectionService.create calls refreshConnectionSchedule only after the callback returns inside AfterCommitService.scope, while outside any scope it calls refreshConnectionSchedule before create resolves.

AC-11 [unit] VcsController.createConnection('s', dto, 'r1'), when findBySlug resolves project p1, calls routeGate.run with { key: 'vcs.connection.create', variant: 'rest:vcs.create', projectId: 'p1', input: { slug: 's', projectId: 'p1', connection: dto }, redeem: 'r1' }.

userStories.title: Gated VCS update and webhook-secret rotation, pinned to the connection
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Gate VCS update and webhook-secret rotation with connection identity fencing and secret-free persisted results.

**Motivation** — These 8 routes take or return a secret, so 5b to 5d-2 left them ungated, and 6a built redeem for them.

**Approach** —
- **VCS update and rotate pin the connection.** The handler reads `vcsService.findByProject(project.id)` before the gate (404 `vcs` as today when none), and the input carries `connectionId`. `VcsConnectionService.update` and `rotateWebhookSecret` gain an optional last parameter `connectionId`: when given and the project's current connection has another id, or none, they throw `NotFoundAppException({}, 'vcs')`. So a connection deleted and recreated between approval and redemption is not changed. The redeeming call re-reads the connection before the gate, so its `connectionId` is the new one and the hash differs: 409 `approvals.redeemMismatch`, and the request stays `approved`. A connection deleted and not recreated answers 404 `vcs` from the handler's read, before the gate. The service-level 404 covers only a swap between that read and the execution (unit-tested).
- **VCS create and update refresh polling after commit.** Both await `this.vcsPollingService.refreshConnectionSchedule(id)` inline today. Inside a redeem execution that call would run before the commit and read the row through another connection. Both call a private `refreshAfterCommit(id)` instead:
  - it defers the refresh with `AfterCommitService.defer` (as 6a's `AgentsService.invalidateAfterCommit` does);
  - when `defer` answers false (no scope open: the immediate path), it awaits the refresh at once, as today;
  - the deferred task catches a refresh error and logs it as a warning through a class logger (`private readonly logger = new Logger(VcsConnectionService.name)`, per `.nax/rules/api-logging.md`), so a failed schedule refresh after commit never turns a redemption that already executed into a 500 that loses the one-time `webhookSecret`. The immediate path keeps today's propagation.

  `committedEffect` is not used: it takes a synchronous effect and would drop the awaited refresh. `VcsConnectionService`'s constructor gains `AfterCommitService` (last), resolved from the global `PermissionsModule`.
- **The encryption key stays a route precondition.** The VCS create and update handlers keep refusing a missing `vcsConfig.encryptionKey` (400 `vcs`) before the gate. The update handler's order is `findBySlug` → key check → `findByProject` → gate, so a missing key answers 400 before a missing connection answers 404. The commands read `this.vcsConfig.encryptionKey` when they run, and throw the same 400 when it is missing then.

US-002 has already introduced AfterCommitService, the refresh helper and create's usage; reuse them and switch update in this story.

| Story | Route | Key | Scope | Variant | Input | `redact` | Run | `toResult` |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| US-003 | `PATCH /projects/:slug/vcs` | `vcs.connection.update` | project | `rest:vcs.update` | `{ slug, projectId, connectionId, patch: parseBody(UpdateVcsConnectionDto, …) }` | `patch.token` → `redactSecret` (absent stays absent) | `vcs.update(projectId, key, patch, connectionId)` | `({ webhookSecret, ...rest }) => rest` |
| US-003 | `POST /projects/:slug/vcs/webhook-secret/rotate` | `vcs.webhook-secret.rotate` | project | `rest:vcs.rotate-webhook-secret` | `{ slug, projectId, connectionId }` | none | `vcs.rotateWebhookSecret(projectId, connectionId)` | `() => ({ rotated: true })` |

`key` in the VCS rows is `this.vcsConfig.encryptionKey`, read when the command runs. The VCS rotate route has no body. Its stored input is `{ slug, projectId, connectionId }`, so a redemption matches when the connection is still the one read before the gate. Each handler keeps its `@Requires`, `@HttpCode` and `@ApiResponse`s. It gains `@ApprovalGated({ redeem: true })` and an `@ApprovalRedeemHeader() redeem?: string` parameter (last; `approvals/route/approval-redeem-header.decorator.ts`, as 6a's handlers use: `@Headers(APPROVAL_REDEEM_HEADER)` would make swagger document a second, required header).

Extend VCS_ROUTE_VARIANTS.update/.rotateWebhookSecret and their registry commands, using the upstream redactSecret helper without inserting an absent token key. Preserve successful immediate callers and generated webhookSecret when enabling webhook sync on a legacy row. Update VCS controller gate doubles: rest:vcs.update calls mockVcsService.update(input.projectId, encryptionKey, input.patch), and rest:vcs.rotate-webhook-secret calls mockVcsService.rotateWebhookSecret(input.projectId), exactly those legacy mock arguments rather than connectionId; give findByProject a default resolved connection. Real commands must pass connectionId to the real service. Apply the same update double adjustment in test/integration/vcs/vcs-controller.spec.ts, with default { id: 'conn-1' }, and make its missing-connection case reject from findByProject rather than update. Update the existing project-admin agent rotation case in both vcs-webhook-secret.integration.spec.ts and vcs-permissions.integration.spec.ts to expect 202, approve as root, redeem and run original persistence/secret assertions on the 200 response; keep 403 guard cases unchanged. Extend the upstream-created test/integration/vcs/gated-vcs-secret-routes.integration.spec.ts; it is not a new output here. Each test creates its own connection with the root token, and agents hold project.read, vcs.connection.update and vcs.webhook-secret.rotate on the test project. Remove only PATCH /projects/:slug/vcs and POST /projects/:slug/vcs/webhook-secret/rotate from both rollout lists and set exact contract counts/titles to pending 4/gated 122.

**Scope** — In: update/rotate redeem commands, pre-gate and execution identity checks, update's deferred polling, legacy callers and the 4/122 checkpoint. Out: replacing US-002's helper/create implementation, webhook URL preparation (US-004), invite routing (US-005), project CI-token command (US-006), final allowlist deletion/OpenAPI regeneration (US-007).

**Interface** — `VcsController.updateConnection(slug, dto, redeem?)`; `rotateWebhookSecret(ctx, redeem?)`; `VcsConnectionService.update(…, connectionId?)`; `.rotateWebhookSecret(projectId, connectionId?)`; `VCS_ROUTE_VARIANTS.update`, `.rotateWebhookSecret`.

AC-2 [integration] When an approved VCS update request for { syncMode: 'polling' } is redeemed, then it answers 200 with data.syncMode polling and the request row is executed.

AC-3 [integration] When an agent opens PATCH /api/projects/<slug>/vcs with { token: 'tok-new' }, then input.patch.token is stored as '<redacted>'; approving and redeeming that request answers 200 and its stored encryptedToken decrypts to tok-new.

AC-8 [integration] Given an approved rotate request whose connection was deleted and recreated, when it is redeemed, then it answers 409 with key approvals.redeemMismatch, the request stays approved, and the new connection's webhookSecret is unchanged.
AC-9 [integration] When PATCH /api/projects/<slug>/vcs and POST /api/projects/<slug>/vcs/webhook-secret/rotate use the root token, then each answers 200 and writes no ApprovalRequest row.

AC-10 [unit] VcsConnectionService.update('p1', key, dto, 'c-other') throws NotFoundAppException with key vcs and never calls updateVcsConnection when the current connection id is c1; with connectionId c1 or omitted it updates.
AC-11 [unit] VcsConnectionService.rotateWebhookSecret('p1', 'c-other') throws NotFoundAppException with key vcs and never calls updateVcsConnection when the current connection id is c1.

AC-13 [unit] VcsController.updateConnection('s', dto, 'r1') calls findByProject before routeGate.run and passes the connection id as input.connectionId; a findByProject 404 rejects before routeGate.run, and an empty encryptionKey rejects with 400 vcs without calling findByProject.

AC-14 [integration] Given a connection with webhookSecret null in the database, when an approved { syncMode: 'webhook' } update request is redeemed, then it answers 200 with a non-empty data.webhookSecret and the request row's result has no webhookSecret property.

AC-15 [unit] Inside AfterCommitService.scope, VcsConnectionService.update calls refreshConnectionSchedule only after the scope callback returns; when that deferred refresh rejects, the scope resolves with the update result and its webhookSecret intact, and the class logger's warn is called once.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Gate project webhook creation/update and move outbound URL validation before the redemption transaction.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Gate invite create/resend through redeem, retaining raw invite links only in caller responses and excluding locale from approval hashes.

**Motivation** — These 8 routes take or return a secret, so 5b to 5d-2 left them ungated, and 6a built redeem for them.

**Approach** —
- **The `accept-language` header documentation is left alone.** The invite handlers' `@Headers('accept-language')` already makes `openapi.json` list a required `accept-language` header. US-007 AC-4 counts only `X-Koda-Approval-Request` parameters, so that pre-existing entry does not fail it.

The invite email is sent inside the redeem transaction, as today's code does inline, so `emailed` stays accurate. The rare case is accepted: the settle step rolls back after the email went out, which leaves a sent email with a dead link.

userStories.title: The CI-token project patch through the redeem path
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Remove the CI-token approval bypass and accept mixed project patches through a secret-aware redeem variant.

**Motivation** — So an agent can change the token under any policy, and nobody can change the token and another setting in one call.

**Approach** —
- **`ciWebhookToken: null` (clearing the token) is not a secret.** `redactSecret(null)` is `null`, so a clear is stored as-is. It still takes the redeem variant, as any patch carrying the field does, so one route has one variant per shape.
- **The project PATCH keeps two variants.** A patch without `ciWebhookToken` keeps `rest:projects.update` (unchanged, a normal deferred command, and its `parse` still refuses `ciWebhookToken` as defence in depth). A patch with it uses the new `rest:projects.update-ci-token` redeem command under the same key `project.update`. The controller picks the variant and passes the header only to the redeem variant. The mixed-patch 400 and the token-only bypass are deleted.

| Story | Route | Key | Scope | Variant | Input | `redact` | Run | `toResult` |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| US-006 | `PATCH /projects/:slug` (with `ciWebhookToken`) | `project.update` | project | `rest:projects.update-ci-token` | `{ slug, patch: parseBody(UpdateProjectDto, …) }` | `patch.ciWebhookToken` → `redactSecret` | `projects.update(slug, patch)` | `(result) => result` |

The project PATCH handler (US-006):

```ts
const { slug: parsedSlug } = parseRouteInput({ slug }, ['slug']);
const patch = parseBody(UpdateProjectDto, updateProjectDto ?? {});
const secret = patch.ciWebhookToken !== undefined;
const outcome = await this.routeGate.run<ProjectResponseDto>({
  key: 'project.update',
  variant: secret ? PROJECT_ROUTE_VARIANTS.updateCiToken : PROJECT_ROUTE_VARIANTS.update,
  projectId: project.project.id,
  input: { slug: parsedSlug, patch },
  ...(secret ? { redeem } : {}),
});
```

A header sent on a patch without `ciWebhookToken` is ignored. The patch then takes the ordinary variant, as any non-redeem gated route ignores the header.

Each handler keeps its `@Requires`, `@HttpCode` and `@ApiResponse`s. It gains `@ApprovalGated({ redeem: true })` and an `@ApprovalRedeemHeader() redeem?: string` parameter (last; `approvals/route/approval-redeem-header.decorator.ts`, as 6a's handlers use: `@Headers(APPROVAL_REDEEM_HEADER)` would make swagger document a second, required header).

Extend PROJECT_ROUTE_VARIANTS with updateCiToken and register its redeem command in the existing ProjectRouteCommands using parseRouteInput/parseBody and the shared redactSecret. Preserve the ordinary update command unchanged, including approvals.invalidInput for ciWebhookToken. Use the same project.update key and scope and projects.update service; no service bypass remains in the controller. Both a token-only and a mixed token/ordinary patch form one redeem request when an agent meets a policy. Humans execute immediately under the policy; agents execute immediately without policy because project.update remains medium/default none. Clear null is accepted and remains null through redaction. After routeGate.run, throw ApprovalPending on pending and return JsonResponse.Ok(outcome.result) on executed. Extend project-route.commands.spec.ts with registration, redaction and null cases while retaining ordinary parse refusal. Replace projects.controller.spec.ts's token-only bypass it.each and mixed-patch rejection it.each with variant/header-routing assertions. Add test/integration/projects/gated-project-ci-token-route.integration.spec.ts, using project.read and project.update bindings on the test project and seedWaitPolicy for wait cases. Preserve ordinary deferred execution on approval when no ciWebhookToken is provided, even if a redemption header was supplied. No new gated route is counted here: checkpoint remains pending 0/gated 126.

**Scope** — In: token-bearing and mixed project PATCH behavior, variant selection, secret/null hashing and ordinary-path regressions. Out: invite gates/locale (US-005), final allowlist deletion/OpenAPI artifact (US-007), changing project.update defaults or the CI-token read route.

**Interface** — `ProjectsController.update(slug, dto, project, redeem?)`; `PROJECT_ROUTE_VARIANTS.updateCiToken`; `rest:projects.update-ci-token`; existing `rest:projects.update` parse remains unchanged.
